current_example.title: Example: Finding the Formula for the Nth Term Given Another Term and the Common Difference

q-5288.name: Question 1
q-5288.problem: Find the formula for the $n$th term of an arithmetic sequence if the first term is $5$ and the common difference is $1.$
q-5288.worked_solution:
The formula for the $n$th term of an arithmetic sequence is

$$
{a}_{n}={a}_{1}+(n-1)d.
$$

We are told that the first term is ${a}_{1}=5$ and the common difference is $d=1.$ So, we substitute into the formula and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}+(n-1)d \\  & =5+(n-1)(1) \\  & =5+n-1 \\  & =4+n\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore the formula for the $n$th term is ${a}_{n}=4+n.$

q-5288.html:
Question 1
?

Find the formula for the nth term of an arithmetic sequence if the first term is 5 and the common difference is 1.

a
an=5n−4
b
an=4+n
c
an=−5n−4
d
an=n−1
e
an=5n−5
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The formula for the nth term of an arithmetic sequence is

an=a1+(n−1)d.

We are told that the first term is a1=5 and the common difference is d=1. So, we substitute into the formula and simplify:

an=a1+(n−1)d=5+(n−1)(1)=5+n−1=4+n

Therefore the formula for the nth term is an=4+n.

q-214167.problem:
Find the formula for the $n$th term of an arithmetic sequence if the first term is $3$ and the second term is $9.$

{{field-1}}

q-214167.worked_solution:
The formula for the $n$th term of an arithmetic sequence is

$$
{a}_{n}={a}_{1}+(n-1)d.
$$

We are given the first term ${a}_{1}=3.$ Also, the common difference of the sequence can be found as

$$
d=9-3=6.
$$

$$

$$

q-5284.name: Question 3
q-5284.problem:
Find the general formula  for the $n$th term of an arithmetic sequence that begins with 

$$
8,\,4,\,0,\,…
$$
q-5284.worked_solution:
The formula for the $n$th term of an arithmetic sequence (in function notation) is

$$
f(n)=f(1)+(n-1)d.
$$

From the first few terms

$$
8,\,4,\,0,\,…,
$$

we see that the first term is $f(1)=8$ and the common difference is 

$$
d=4-8=-4.
$$

So, we substitute into the formula and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(n) & =f(1)+(n-1)d \\  & =8+(n-1)(-4) \\  & =8-4n+4 \\  & =12-4n\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the formula for the $n$th term is $f(n)=12-4n.$

q-5284.html:
Question 3
?

Find the general formula for the nth term of an arithmetic sequence that begins with 8,4,0,…

a
f(n)=8−8n
b
f(n)=8+4n
c
f(n)=12−4n
d
f(n)=4−4n
e
f(n)=0
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The formula for the nth term of an arithmetic sequence (in function notation) is

f(n)=f(1)+(n−1)d.

From the first few terms

8,4,0,…,

we see that the first term is f(1)=8 and the common difference is d=4−8=−4.

So, we substitute into the formula and simplify:

f(n)=f(1)+(n−1)d=8+(n−1)(−4)=8−4n+4=12−4n

Therefore, the formula for the nth term is f(n)=12−4n.

q-76514.name: Question 4
q-76514.problem: Find the formula for the $n$th term of an arithmetic sequence if the first term is $4$ and the second term is $-2.$
q-76514.worked_solution:
The formula for the $n$th term of an arithmetic sequence (in function notation) is

$$
f(n)=f(1)+(n-1)d.
$$

We are given the first term $f(1)=4.$ Also, the common difference of the sequence can be found as

$$
d=-2-4=-6.
$$

So, we substitute into the formula and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(n) & =f(1)+(n-1)d \\  & =4+(n-1)(-6) \\  & =4-6n+6 \\  & =10-6n\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the formula for the $n$th term is $f(n)=10-6n.$

q-76514.html:
Question 4
?

Find the formula for the nth term of an arithmetic sequence if the first term is 4 and the second term is −2.

a
f(n)=−2+6n
b
f(n)=10−6n
c
f(n)=2−6n
d
f(n)=6−2n
e
f(n)=10−2n
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The formula for the nth term of an arithmetic sequence (in function notation) is

f(n)=f(1)+(n−1)d.

We are given the first term f(1)=4. Also, the common difference of the sequence can be found as d=−2−4=−6.

So, we substitute into the formula and simplify:

f(n)=f(1)+(n−1)d=4+(n−1)(−6)=4−6n+6=10−6n

Therefore, the formula for the nth term is f(n)=10−6n.
q-76514.knowledge_point: Finding the Formula for the Nth Term of an Arithmetic Sequence in Function Notation

q-214183.name: Question 5
q-214183.problem:
Consider the following arithmetic sequence.

$$
7,\,3,\,-1,\,-5,\,…
$$

What is the $34$th term of this sequence?

${a}_{34}=$
{{field-1}}
q-214183.worked_solution:
The formula for the $n$th term of an arithmetic sequence is

$$
{a}_{n}={a}_{1}+(n-1)d.
$$

First, we will write the formula for the $n$th term of this sequence. From the first few terms

$$
7,\,3,\,-1,\,-5,\,…,
$$

we see that the first term is ${a}_{1}=7$ and the common difference is 

$$
d=3-7=-4.
$$

So, we substitute into the formula and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}+(n-1)d \\  & =7+(n-1)(-4) \\  & =7-4n+4 \\  & =11-4n\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can use our formula to find the $34$th term. All we have to do is substitute $n=34:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & =11-4n \\ {a}_{34} & =11-4(34) \\  & =11-136 \\  & =-125\end{aligned}
$$

q-236631.name: Question 6
q-236631.problem:
Consider the following arithmetic sequence.

$$
-13,\,-9,\,-5,\,-1,\,…
$$

What is the $36$th term of this sequence?

${a}_{36}=$
{{field-1}}
q-236631.worked_solution:
The formula for the $n$th term of an arithmetic sequence is

$$
{a}_{n}={a}_{1}+(n-1)d.
$$

First, we will write the formula for the $n$th term of this sequence. From the first few terms

$$
-13,\,-9,\,-5,\,-1,\,…,
$$

we see that the first term is ${a}_{1}=-13$ and the common difference is 

$$
d=-9-(-13)=4.
$$

So, we substitute into the formula and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}+(n-1)d \\  & =-13+(n-1)(4) \\  & =-13+4n-4 \\  & =4n-17\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can use our formula to find the $36$th term. All we have to do is substitute $n=36:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & =4n-17 \\ {a}_{36} & =4(36)-17 \\  & =144-17 \\  & =127\end{aligned}
$$

q-76518.name: Question 7
q-76518.problem: Given an arithmetic sequence that has ${a}_{8}=8$ and the common difference $d=4$, what is the general formula for the $n$th term of the sequence?
q-76518.worked_solution:
Since ${a}_{8}=8$ is $7$ jumps after ${a}_{1},$ we can determine the first term of the sequence:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{8} & ={a}_{1}+7d \\ 8 & ={a}_{1}+7(4) \\ 8 & ={a}_{1}+28 \\ -20 & ={a}_{1}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the formula for the $n$th term is:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}+(n-1)d \\  & =-20+(n-1)(4) \\  & =-20+4n-4 \\  & =4n-24\end{aligned}
$$

q-76518.html:
Question 7
?

Given an arithmetic sequence that has a8=8 and the common difference d=4, what is the general formula for the nth term of the sequence?

a
an=4n−24
b
an=−4n+40
c
an=4n−28
d
an=4n−20
e
an=−4n+36
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Since a8=8 is 7 jumps after a1, we can determine the first term of the sequence:

a8=a1+7d8=a1+7(4)8=a1+28−20=a1

So, the formula for the nth term is:

an=a1+(n−1)d=−20+(n−1)(4)=−20+4n−4=4n−24
q-76518.knowledge_point: Finding the Formula for the Nth Term Given Another Term and the Common Difference

q-236649.name: Question 8
q-236649.problem:
Find the formula for the $n$th term of the arithmetic sequence that has ${a}_{25}=95$ and the common difference $d=4.$

${a}_{n}=$
{{field-1}}$,\,n\ge 1$
q-236649.worked_solution:
Since ${a}_{25}=95$ is $24$ jumps after ${a}_{1},$ we can determine the first term of the sequence:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{25} & ={a}_{1}+24d \\ 95 & ={a}_{1}+24(4) \\ 95 & ={a}_{1}+96 \\ -1 & ={a}_{1}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the formula for the $n$th term is:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}+(n-1)d \\  & =-1+(n-1)(4) \\  & =-1+4n-4 \\  & =4n-5\end{aligned}
$$
